definition: A platform where ad buyers purchase ad inventory across multiple media and manage bidding, targeting, and performance.
example: In the DSP, I set the campaign's bid cap and exposure conditions.

definition: A platform where media offer their ad inventory to multiple demand sources and manage sales conditions and revenue.
example: In the SSP, I manage the inventory to sell and the price conditions.

definition: A digital marketplace that connects transactions between buyers and sellers of ad inventory.
example: I check the transaction conditions of the ad exchange.

definition: Advertising composed so its format and usage flow fit with a medium's ordinary content.
example: I mark native advertising so it can still be recognized as an ad.

definition: The scale of ad transactions an agency handled over a defined period. It is distinguished from commission revenue or net profit.
example: I report billing separately from agency revenue.

definition: A medium or system that displays guidance, information, and advertising content on electronic displays.
example: I set the playback schedule for the store's digital signage.

definition: A method of wrapping the surface of a vehicle or facility with advertising graphics and the like for exposure.
example: I check the actual application area of the bus wrap advertising.

definition: A token format that conveys claims, which are information about a subject, in a compact JSON-based form. Signing and encryption must be distinguished.
example: Before trusting the values in a JWT, I check the verification procedure.
note: Base64url encoding is not encryption. The contents of a signed JWT do not automatically become secret.

definition: An authorization framework that lets an application receive limited access to resources on behalf of a user.
example: I limit the access scope requested in OAuth to the necessary level.
note: OAuth itself handles authorization. A separate authentication layer such as OpenID Connect may be used to verify user identity.

definition: A family of databases centered on data models other than relational tables, such as document, key-value, and graph.
example: I review a NoSQL model that fits the data access patterns.
note: It does not mean there is no schema at all. Structure, validation, and transaction features differ by product and data model.

definition: A structure that gathers and manages connections so multiple tasks can reuse them.
example: I check the connection pool's wait time and the number of connections in use.

definition: A logically isolated network space in the cloud and its configuration.
example: I design the VPC's subnets and access paths.

definition: A feature that automatically increases or decreases the number or size of computing resources according to load or defined conditions.
example: I set the autoscaling minimum and maximum capacity.

definition: A setting that forwards communication arriving at a specific address and port to another address and port.
example: I check the destination address and port of the port forwarding.

definition: The work of managing how the state used by screens and features is stored, changed, and shared.
example: When multiple screens use the same value, I define the state-management scope.

definition: A rendering method that generates the screen's HTML on the server and sends it to the client.
example: In SSR, I check the initial response time and the caching strategy.

definition: A rendering method that runs code on the client, such as the browser, to compose the screen.
example: In CSR, I prepare the initial loading and error states.

definition: A browser component that displays and runs web content inside an app.
example: I check the navigation and back behavior between the WebView and the app.

definition: An application built on the features and runtime environment of a specific operating system.
example: In the native app, I check the platform's accessibility features.

definition: An approach that uses shared code and technology so it runs on multiple operating systems or platforms.
example: Even when built cross-platform, I verify the behavior on each platform.

definition: A method of loading resources or features when needed rather than all at once from the start.
example: I apply lazy loading to images below the fold.

definition: A vulnerability revealed while the provider is unaware of it or has not had enough time to respond.
example: I check the impact scope and response guidance in the zero-day vulnerability notice.
note: Distinguish the vulnerability, the attack that exploits it, and the disclosure timing of the fix patch. Not every unpatched old vulnerability is called a zero-day.

definition: A test that checks a system's limits, failure, and recovery characteristics under load or constraint conditions beyond the expected range.
example: In the stress test, I also check whether it recovers after failure.

definition: A deployment method that applies a new version while avoiding interruption to users' service.
example: For zero-downtime deployment, I check compatibility of existing requests and data.

definition: A procedure in which an app or update is reviewed for whether it meets the distribution platform's requirements.
example: I prepare the description and test account needed for app review.

definition: A field expression for a submitted deliverable not being approved but turned back in app review and the like.
example: I read the rejection reasons and prepare the needed fixes and explanations.

definition: The source of information designated as the reference when many people consult it. It does not necessarily mean putting all data in one file.
example: I define the SSOT for pricing information to reduce discrepancies across duplicate documents.

definition: A marker indicating that something is not yet decided and must be decided later.
example: I mark items whose schedule is not finalized as TBD.

definition: A marker indicating that content will be announced or notified later.
example: I announce the event location as TBA.

definition: A phenomenon in which the scope of work gradually grows without adjusting schedule, cost, or resources, or without change management.
example: To prevent scope creep, I check the impact of additional requests.

definition: An effort unit based on the amount of work one person performs in one month.
example: I distinguish the man-month estimate from the actual calendar duration.
note: It is a unit of work. It does not mean that doubling the number of people necessarily halves the duration.

definition: The process of organizing and concluding a meeting's or project's results, decisions, and remaining tasks.
example: In the wrap-up, I check the follow-up actions per owner.

definition: A casual, informal conversation or meeting to exchange information about work, career, and the like.
example: Before the coffee chat, I organize the work questions I'm curious about.

definition: A finishing process, mainly on cotton, that treats the fiber with alkali to change properties such as luster and dyeability.
example: I compare the luster and hand before and after mercerization.

definition: A method of printing an image directly onto a garment's surface by inkjet.
example: I check the color and post-wash condition of the DTG sample.

definition: A printing method that uses heat to transfer sublimating dyes onto suitable materials such as polyester to produce color.
example: I first check whether the blend ratio is suitable for dye sublimation.
note: Dye sublimation requires suitable dyes and materials. It is not the same process as all heat transfer or pigment printing.

definition: A finishing process that stabilizes fabric in advance to reduce shrinkage during washing or use.
example: Even after anti-shrink finishing, I test against the target shrinkage rate.
note: Sanforizing is one anti-shrink method that uses compressive shrinkage. Do not treat it as synonymous with all anti-shrink finishing.

definition: A property that keeps water from spreading or soaking in easily on a surface, instead beading up and rolling off.
example: I compare the water-repellency performance before and after washing.
note: Water repellency alone does not guarantee waterproofing against water pressure.

definition: The performance of preventing water from penetrating into a material or product under defined use and test conditions.
example: I check not only the waterproof fabric but also the seam treatment.
note: It does not mean completely blocking water under any pressure or duration. Distinguish the test conditions for the material and the finished product.

definition: A process that washes and treats a garment in its sewn state to adjust its hand, appearance, dimensions, and more.
example: I check the finished dimensions after garment washing.

definition: A linear-density unit that expresses the mass in grams of 9,000 meters of yarn.
example: Under the same material conditions, I compare the denier and the fabric construction together.
note: It is a mass-per-length unit. Do not conclude fiber quality or fabric thickness from the number alone.

definition: A finishing process that fixes pigment onto the fiber surface with a binder and the like to produce color.
example: I check the rub fastness of pigment-dyed products.

definition: A method of printing by passing ink through a mesh screen that has a pattern formed in it.
example: I check the per-color registration of the screen printing.

definition: A printing method that expresses a pattern by removing the ground color in the pattern areas. It sometimes also renders other colors.
example: I use a sample to check whether the dye and fabric allow discharge printing.
note: It is a process that removes the existing ground color. Distinguish it from high-density printing that builds up thick ink or rubber printing.

definition: A ring-shaped trim that reinforces or decorates the edge of a lace hole, ventilation hole, and the like.
example: I check whether the eyelet's inner diameter matches the lace thickness.

definition: A fastening trim that locks by pressing two interlocking parts together and opens by pulling them apart.
example: I check the snap fastener's holding force and any fabric damage.

definition: A metal trim that joins two parts or reinforces and decorates a stress point.
example: I check the rivet positions on the jeans pockets.

definition: A set of color samples organized to compare color differences in production fabric and the like and judge the tolerance range.
example: I match the color of the cutting bundles against the shade band.

definition: The degree to which fabric withstands bulging or pressing in multiple directions before it bursts.
example: I compare fabrics by matching the bursting-strength test conditions.

definition: The force needed for an already started tear to progress further in the fabric.
example: For tear strength, I check the results by fabric direction.

definition: A print color build that adds other inks to black K ink to express a deep black.
example: I check the ink mix for rich black against the output conditions.
note: There is no fixed all-purpose CMYK mix. Check the paper, print method, and total ink coverage. The claim that 100% K is always a bad black is also incorrect.

definition: Data that describes the color characteristics of a device or color space and is used to interpret and convert color in the color-management process.
example: I check the ICC profile the print shop requested.
note: Attaching a profile alone does not make color exactly the same on every device. Device condition and output conditions also have an effect.

definition: The process of measuring and adjusting a device's output or display state to match a set standard.
example: I set the target brightness and white point for the monitor calibration.

definition: The range of colors a device or color space can express or contain.
example: I check how colors outside the print gamut are converted.

definition: A metric that expresses the difference between two colors numerically. You must check the formula used and the measurement conditions together.
example: I compare the Delta E result together with the actual sample.

definition: A repeating reference line used so that the text baselines across multiple lines and columns align consistently.
example: I align the body text in both columns to the baseline grid.

definition: A form that combines two or more characters into a single glyph.
example: When I turn on ligatures, I check the letter connection and legibility.

definition: A typeface whose expression and proportions are designed for use at large sizes, such as titles.
example: I check whether a display typeface still reads well in body text.

definition: The height of the body based on the lowercase x. It can differ by typeface even at the same font size.
example: I match the sizes of two typefaces, accounting for the x-height difference.

definition: Information and environment design that helps people understand their current location and destination in a space and find their way.
example: In wayfinding, I first inspect the guidance at decision points.

definition: A category that groups furniture, fixtures, equipment, and the like handled in a space project.
example: In the FF&E list, I note the quantity and lead time per item.
note: The included scope differs by contract and project. It is not a list that automatically includes all architectural finishes or decorative items.

definition: A graphic format that describes vector shapes and the like in XML. It can also contain text or raster images.
example: I check the SVG's zoomed state and font rendering.

definition: An image file format for storing raster image data. It can use no compression or several compression methods.
example: When delivering a TIFF, I check the color space and compression settings.

definition: An interface method that keeps loading the next content as scrolling progresses.
example: Even with infinite scroll, I make it easy to find the previous position.

definition: An interface design that misleads users into choices other than what they intend, or makes choices difficult.
example: I review for dark patterns that hide the cancel button.

definition: Apple's codec family used in video editing and post-production. It includes several compression formats that differ in image quality and data volume.
example: For ProRes delivery, I check the codec type and whether an alpha channel is needed.
note: We corrected the original description that it is an uncompressed codec. Not the entire ProRes family supports an alpha channel.

definition: Equipment that blocks unwanted light in front of the lens and lets you mount filters and the like.
example: I check that the matte box does not block the edges of the frame.

definition: A system that programs and precisely repeats the movement of a camera and the like.
example: For compositing, I repeat the same motion-control move.

definition: A vehicle carrying power-generation equipment that supplies the electricity needed for shooting and the like.
example: I check the generator-truck position and power plan with the person in charge.

definition: A furry windscreen cover put over a microphone to reduce the effect of wind.
example: Before outdoor recording, I fit the dead cat and check the sound.
note: It is an accessory that reduces wind effects, not a device that removes all noise.

definition: A shooting stand used to support lighting, flags, reflectors, and the like.
example: I inspect the C-stand setup and load with the person in charge.

definition: An auxiliary counterweight that adds weight to equipment supports and the like to improve stability.
example: I check the sandbag positions to match the setup conditions.

definition: A board or tool that partially blocks light to create patterned shadows such as leaves or windows.
example: I create a shadow pattern on the wall with a cucoloris.

definition: A lighting accessory that passes light through a diffusion surface to make it broad and soft.
example: I adjust the softbox size and distance and examine the shadows.

definition: A tube-shaped lighting accessory and the like that narrows the spread of light.
example: With a snoot, I concentrate light on a small part of the background.

definition: The stage of finalizing the picture edit so it can serve as the basis for subsequent color, sound, and compositing.
example: After picture lock, I also inform the post team of changes along with their impact.
note: It does not mean later changes are physically impossible. If changes are made, re-coordinate the schedule, cost, and versions of the related post work.

definition: Extra frames left before and after the used section for transitions or length adjustment.
example: I deliver each cut to the compositing team with handles included.

definition: An editing method that synchronizes source from multiple cameras shooting the same scene and the like and switches between them.
example: Before multicam editing, I check the sync of each camera.

definition: Footage or an image securing a background without the target person or object, for use as a reference in compositing or removal work.
example: I shoot the clean plate with the actor out of frame.

definition: Data output by separating render-result elements such as lighting, reflection, shadow, and depth.
example: I separate the render passes to adjust them in compositing.

definition: Data containing distance and depth information between the camera and scene elements.
example: I use Z-depth to control fog and depth-of-field effects in compositing.

definition: A phenomenon where the color of the background or surroundings reflects onto and tints the subject.
example: After keying, I check the green spill around the hair.

definition: An audio processing tool that selectively reduces the frequency components where sibilance stands out.
example: While applying the de-esser, I listen to make sure the pronunciation does not become muddy.

definition: A digital work environment for recording and editing audio and placing and mixing music and sound effects.
example: I match the DAW session's sample rate to the project standard.

definition: A submix output by defined audio group, such as dialogue, music, and sound effects.
example: Along with the full mix, I deliver the dialogue, music, and effects stems.

definition: Audio processing that attenuates the signal when it is below a set level to reduce sound.
example: I check that the noise gate does not cut off the ends of words.

definition: A dynamics tool that strongly suppresses signals exceeding a set threshold level.
example: I check the limiter's output ceiling and any distortion together.
note: The threshold is not necessarily 0 dB. The behavior and result vary by measurement basis, settings, and processing method.

definition: A phenomenon where the signal exceeds the processable range and the waveform is cut off and distorted.
example: I monitor for audio clipping during recording.

definition: A tool that adjusts the signal level per frequency band to change the balance of the sound.
example: With EQ, I adjust the bands where the dialogue and music overlap.

definition: A tool that reduces the level of signals exceeding a set threshold according to ratio and time conditions to control the dynamic range.
example: I compare the sound before and after applying the compressor.
note: Automatically boosting quiet sounds is not an essential behavior. Distinguish separate settings such as output make-up gain.

definition: A feature that displays brightness or exposure ranges in different colors to help judge exposure.
example: I check the false-color reference chart and inspect the exposure.
note: The exposure range each color represents varies by equipment, mode, and settings.

definition: The number of bits processed or stored per unit of time. In video, it usually indicates the data volume per second.
example: I check the expected file size from the video length and bitrate.

definition: A method that allocates bitrate differently depending on the section, content, and the like.
example: I check the VBR target and maximum bitrate settings.

definition: A method that allocates data to keep a set bitrate level constant.
example: I check the CBR settings to match the broadcast specs.
note: It does not mean every frame has exactly the same file size.

definition: A format that holds streams and information such as video, audio, and subtitles in a single file structure.
example: I check the media container together with the internal codec.
note: MP4, MOV, and MXF are examples of containers. You cannot tell the codec or quality from the extension alone.

definition: A Google Analytics property type that measures and analyzes website and app usage behavior centered on events.
example: In GA4, I check the purchase events and traffic sources together.

definition: An abbreviation for Naver's performance-based display advertising.
example: I check the goals and performance metrics of the GFA campaign.
note: We linked the Korean official name and its abbreviation. Do not guess the English expansion of the abbreviation without separate evidence.

definition: A method in which, when an ad-impression opportunity arises, buyers bid in real time to determine the transaction conditions.
example: I look at the RTB bidding results together with the actual conversion performance.

definition: Advertising that uses an editorial format such as an article or contributed piece to deliver a product or brand message.
example: I check the ad labeling and the content to convey in the advertorial.

definition: A marketing approach that provides the content and search information customers need so that customers come on their own.
example: In inbound marketing, I prepare content that matches the customer's search intent.

definition: A marketing approach in which a company proactively delivers a message to target customers through advertising, outreach, and the like.
example: I decide the targets and contact methods for outbound marketing.

definition: A presentation and persuasion process that proposes strategy, ideas, and capabilities to an advertiser and the like to win adoption or the contract.
example: In the pitch, I clearly convey the problem definition and the rationale for the proposal.

definition: A method of releasing first on a limited audience, region, or scale and checking the operation and response.
example: Based on the soft-launch results, I adjust the scope of the full release.

definition: Slide material assembled for a presentation, proposal, explanation, and the like.
example: Before the meeting, I check the deck's key message and order.

definition: The perspective, method, or way of tackling a problem or goal.
example: For the same goal, I compare two approaches.

definition: The process of connecting the client's component state and behavior to HTML generated on the server or at build time to make it interactive.
example: During hydration, I check that the server and client initial screens match.

definition: A model of entrusting server-infrastructure operation to a provider and using a managed runtime environment or services.
example: Even in serverless, I check the permissions, cost, and execution limits.
note: It does not mean there are no servers. Nor does it mean the developer no longer manages the application's permissions, configuration, and execution characteristics.

definition: The branch designated as the default baseline in a repository. Names such as main or master are used, but the name and operating rules differ by project.
example: Before merging into the default branch, I check the team's verification procedure.
note: The name main or master does not guarantee a deployable or stable state.

definition: A distributed version-control system that records file change history and manages work with branches, merges, and the like.
example: With Git, I record the reason for changes and the work history.

definition: A platform that hosts Git repositories and provides development-collaboration features such as code review and issues.
example: I review the changes in a GitHub pull request.

definition: A bundle of libraries, tools, documentation, examples, and more provided to develop for or integrate with a specific platform or feature.
example: I check the SDK's supported environments and usage examples.

definition: A method of repeatedly checking at regular intervals and the like whether there is a state change or new data.
example: I adjust the polling interval together with responsiveness and server load.

definition: A record showing the function call path at a specific moment. It is used to trace the location and circumstances of an error.
example: In the stack trace, I check the call flow just before the error.

definition: A state or error in which available memory is insufficient and the required memory cannot be secured.
example: When OOM occurs, I check the memory limit and usage pattern.
note: It means a state of insufficient memory, and the result is not always a forced process termination.

definition: Fictional data prepared for use in development, testing, screen checks, and the like.
example: I include empty values and long names in the dummy data to check the screen.
note: Distinguish it from a dummy object, a test double that only fills a slot and is not used.

definition: The work of designing wording such as buttons, guidance, and error messages so users can understand the product and act.
example: In UX writing, I briefly explain the cause of the error and the next action.

definition: The depth of the hierarchy descending from upper items to lower items in a menu or information structure.
example: I check that the depth of frequently sought information is not too deep.

definition: A screen shown briefly while an app or program prepares its initial screen at startup.
example: I make the splash screen transition naturally into the main screen.

definition: The overall impression and usage sensation of a product or interface felt through its color, typeface, layout, and motion.
example: I check whether the new screen's look and feel is consistent with the existing product.

definition: A small icon displayed to identify a website in browser tabs, bookmarks, and the like.
example: I check that the favicon is distinguishable even at a small size.
note: The display position and size differ by browser. It is not an element fixed to the right side of the tab.
